70292-least-said-soonest-mended.title: Soonest Mended.
70292-least-said-soonest-mended.creator: Agnes Giberne,
70292-least-said-soonest-mended.description: A book by Agnes Giberne,. I think I see her now—middle-aged, and going on for plumpness, with smooth brown hair, and a smooth forehead, and such a pair of quick eyes. Mother's eyes did a lot of speaking, when her lips were silent. Nothing ever escaped those eyes. She didn't always talk about what she saw, and she didn't forget it.

7282-the-captivi-and-the-mostellaria.title: The Captivi And The Mostellaria
7282-the-captivi-and-the-mostellaria.creator: Unknown
7282-the-captivi-and-the-mostellaria.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. two sons; a slave stole one child when four years old, and flying hence, he sold him in Elis [2], to the father of this _captive_ (_pointing to_ PHILOCRATES). Now, do you understand this? I' faith, that man at a distance [3] there (_pointing_) says, no.

arxiv-2012-05046.title: A multi-objective optimization framework for online ridesharing systems* This document is the results of the research project funded by Ford Motor company.
arxiv-2012-05046.creator: Hamed Javidi, Dan Simon, Ling Zhu, Yan Wang
arxiv-2012-05046.description: Abstract The ultimate goal of ridesharing systems is to match travelers who do not have a vehicle with those travelers who want to share their vehicle. A good match can be found among those who have similar itineraries and time schedules.

arxiv-2305-06798.title: Vibrations and tunneling of strained nanoribbons at finite temperature
arxiv-2305-06798.creator: Paul Z. Hanakata, Sourav S. Bhabesh, David Yllanes, David R. Nelson, Mark J. Bowick
arxiv-2305-06798.description: Abstract Crystalline sheets (e.g., graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides) liberated from a substrate are a paradigm for materials at criticality because flexural phonons can fluctuate into the third dimension. Although studies of static critical behaviors (e.g., the scale-dependent elastic constants) are plentiful, investigations of dynamics remain limited.

arxiv-2307-02389.title: A remark on the quantum complexity of the Kronecker coefficients
arxiv-2307-02389.creator: Christian Ikenmeyer and Sathyawageeswar Subramanian
arxiv-2307-02389.description: Abstract We prove that the computation of the Kronecker coefficients of the symmetric group is contained in the complexity class #BQP . This improves a recent result of Bravyi, Chowdhury, Gosset, Havlicek, and Zhu. We use only the quantum computing tools that are used in their paper and additional classical representation theoretic insights.

arxiv-2402-17738.title: Observation of the \PGXmb → \PGyP ​ 2 ​ S ​ \PGXm \PGXmb\to\PGyP{2S}\PGXm decay and studies of the \HepParticleResonanceFull \PGX b59450 \Xspace baryon in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2402-17738.description: Abstract The first observation of the decay \PGXmb → \PGyP ​ 2 ​ S ​ \PGXm \PGXmb\to\PGyP{2S}\PGXm and measurement of the branching ratio of \PGXmb → \PGyP ​ 2 ​ S ​ \PGXm \PGXmb\to\PGyP{2S}\PGXm to \PGXmb → \PJGy ​ \PGXm \PGXmb\to\PJGy\PGXm are presented.

arxiv-2403-03789.title: Recovering orthogonality from quasi-nature of Spectral transformations
arxiv-2403-03789.creator: VIKASH KUMAR †, Francisco Marcellán ††, A. Swaminathan †††
arxiv-2403-03789.description: Abstract . In this contribution, quasi-orthogonality of polynomials generated by Geronimus and Uvarov transformations is analyzed. An attempt is made to discuss the recovery of the source orthogonal polynomial from the quasi-Geronimus and quasi-Uvarov polynomials of order one. Moreover, the discussion on the difference equation satisfied by quasi-Geronimus and quasi-Uvarov polynomials is presented.

arxiv-2411-17495.title: A Machine Learning-based Anomaly Detection Framework in Life Insurance Contracts
arxiv-2411-17495.creator: Andreas Groll, Akshat Khanna, Leonid Zeldin
arxiv-2411-17495.description: Abstract Life insurance, like other forms of insurance, relies heavily on large volumes of data. The business model is based on an exchange where companies receive payments in return for the promise to provide coverage in case of an accident. Thus, trust in the integrity of the data stored in databases is crucial.

arxiv-2412-06061.title: Curse of Attention: A Kernel-Based Perspective for Why Transformers Fail to Generalize on Time Series Forecasting and Beyond
arxiv-2412-06061.creator: Yekun Ke, Yingyu Liang, Zhenmei Shi, Zhao Song, Chiwun Yang
arxiv-2412-06061.description: Abstract The application of transformer-based models on time series forecasting (TSF) tasks has long been popular to study. However, many of these works fail to beat the simple linear residual model, and the theoretical understanding of this issue is still limited. In this work, we propose the first theoretical explanation of the inefficiency of transformers on TSF tasks.

arxiv-2502-18969.title: (Mis)Fitting: A Survey of Scaling Laws Thanks: Equal contribution
arxiv-2502-18969.creator: Margaret Li*, Sneha Kudugunta*, Luke Zettlemoyer
arxiv-2502-18969.description: Abstract Modern foundation models rely heavily on using scaling laws to guide crucial training decisions. Researchers often extrapolate the optimal architecture and hyper parameters settings from smaller training runs by describing the relationship between, loss, or task performance, and scale. All components of this process vary, from the specific equation being fit, to the training setup, to the optimization method.

arxiv-2504-16059.title: Sub-Horizon Amplification of Curvature Perturbations: A New Route to Primordial Black Holes and Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2504-16059.creator: and Arnab Sarkar
arxiv-2504-16059.description: Abstract The enhanced primordial scalar power spectrum is a widely studied mechanism for generating primordial gravitational waves (PGWs), also referred to as scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs). This process also plays a pivotal role in facilitating the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). Traditionally, the ultra slow-roll (USR) mechanism has been the predominant approach used in the early universe.

arxiv-2505-01652.title: Causally Fair Node Classification on Non-IID Graph Data
arxiv-2505-01652.creator: Yucong Dai yucongd@clemson.edu, Lu Zhang lz006@uark.edu, Yaowei Hu yaowei.hu@walmart.com, Susan Gauch sgauch@uark.edu, Yongkai Wu yongkaw@clemson.edu
arxiv-2505-01652.description: Abstract Fair machine learning seeks to identify and mitigate biases in predictions against unfavorable populations characterized by demographic attributes, such as race and gender. Recent research has extended fairness to graph data, such as social networks, but many studies neglect the causal relationships among data instances.

arxiv-2505-15280.title: Multisetting protocol for Bell correlated states detection with spin- f f systems
arxiv-2505-15280.creator: Arkadiusz Kobus, Xinwei Li, Mariusz Gajda, Li You, Emilia Witkowska
arxiv-2505-15280.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arkadiusz Kobus, Xinwei Li, Mariusz Gajda, Li You, Emilia Witkowska. We propose a multisetting protocol for the detection of two-body Bell correlations, and apply it to spin-nematic squeezed states realized in f f pairs of SU(2) subsystems within spin- f f atomic Bose–Einstein condensates. Experimental data for f = 1 f=1 , together with numerical simulations using the truncated Wigner method for f = 1 , 2 , 3 f=1,\,2,\,3 , demonstrate the protocol’s effectiveness.

arxiv-2508-17863.title: Speech Discrete Tokens or Continuous Features? A Comparative Analysis for Spoken Language Understanding in SpeechLLMs
arxiv-2508-17863.creator: Dingdong Wang, Junan Li, Mingyu Cui, Dongchao Yang, Xueyuan Chen, Helen Meng
arxiv-2508-17863.description: Abstract With the rise of Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs), two dominant approaches have emerged for speech processing: discrete tokens and continuous features. Each approach has demonstrated strong capabilities in audio-related processing tasks. However, the performance gap between these two paradigms has not been thoroughly explored.

arxiv-2508-20951.title: A local and nonlocal coupling model involving the p p -Laplacian Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Clasification . 35R11, 45K05, 47G20. Thanks: Key words and phrases . Local equations, nonlocal equations, p p -Laplacian Thanks: Partially supported by Secyt-UNC grant CB33620180100016
arxiv-2508-20951.creator: Uriel Kaufmann, Raúl Vidal
arxiv-2508-20951.description: Abstract In this paper we extend some results presented in [ 1 ] to the case of the p p -Laplacian operator. More precisely, we consider a model that couples a local p p -Laplacian operator with a nonlocal p p -Laplacian operator through source terms in the equation. The resulting problem is associated with an energy functional.

arxiv-2509-14438.title: Simulating a Bias Mitigation Scenario in Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-14438.creator: Kiana Kiashemshaki, Mohammad Jalili Torkamani, Negin Mahmoudi, Meysam Shirdel Bilehsavar
arxiv-2509-14438.description: Abstract Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have fundamentally transformed the field of natural language processing; however, their vulnerability to biases presents a notable obstacle that threatens both fairness and trust. This review offers an extensive analysis of the bias landscape in LLMs, tracing its roots and expressions across various NLP tasks.

arxiv-2510-25630.title: Average Rank of Elliptic Curves Over Function Fields
arxiv-2510-25630.creator: ırmak Balçık
arxiv-2510-25630.description: Abstract . Let q q be a prime with q ≥ 5 q\geq 5 . We show that the average rank of elliptic curves over a function field 𝔽 q ​ ( t ) \mathbb{F}_{q}(t) , when ordered by naive height, is bounded above by 25 / 14 ≈ 1.8 25/14\approx 1.8 .

arxiv-2606-19015.creator: Sushil Pandit

doe-osti-3013883-enabling-efficient-spar.title: Enabling Efficient Sparse Computations using Linear Algebra Aware Compilers
doe-osti-3013883-enabling-efficient-spar.creator: Rajamanickam, Sivasankaran, Kelley, Brian Michael, Sadayappan, Ponnuswamy et al.
doe-osti-3013883-enabling-efficient-spar.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. This project developed the LAPIS compiler framework, built on the Multilevel Intermediate Representation (MLIR), to optimize sparse linear algebra operations and support performance portability across diverse architectures. The main innovation of LAPIS is the Kokkos dialect, whic

europmc-pmc517706.title: MUSCLE: a multiple sequence alignment method with reduced time and space complexity.
europmc-pmc517706.creator: Edgar RC.
europmc-pmc517706.description: Background In a previous paper, we introduced MUSCLE, a new program for creating multiple alignments of protein sequences, giving a brief summary of the algorithm and showing MUSCLE to achieve the highest scores reported to date on four alignment accuracy benchmarks....

pmc-11305429.title: Peripheral Ganglion Cell Complex Thickness and Retinal Microvasculature in Myopia Using Wide-Field Swept-Source OCT
pmc-11305429.creator: Deming Wang, Yinhang Zhang, Fengbin Lin, Yunhe Song, Ling Jin, Zhenyu Wang, Meiling Chen, Jiaxuan Jiang, Peiyuan Wang, Zefeng Yang, Shaojie Yuan, Xiulan Zhang
pmc-11305429.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeThis study aims to investigate the impact of axial elongation on ganglion cell complex thickness (GCCT) and retinal capillary density (CD) using wide-field swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography.MethodsA retrospective cross-sectional analysis was conducted involving 506 eyes.

pmc-11437731.title: Eales’ disease with secondary coats’-like reaction: a case report
pmc-11437731.creator: Chien Xue Low, Shelina Oli Mohamed, Mimiwati Zahari
pmc-11437731.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundEales’ disease is an idiopathic, inflammatory condition characterized by peripheral retinal phlebitis, distal non-perfusion, and neovascularization. Coats’ disease, on the other hand, is an idiopathic, retinal vasculopathy characterized by telangiectasia and yellowish exudation. Both diseases commonly affect males.

pmc-11455883.title: Unsupervised few shot learning architecture for diagnosis of periodontal disease in dental panoramic radiographs
pmc-11455883.creator: Min Joo Kim, Sun Geu Chae, Suk Joo Bae, Kyung-Gyun Hwang
pmc-11455883.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In the domain of medical imaging, the advent of deep learning has marked a significant progression, particularly in the nuanced area of periodontal disease diagnosis. This study specifically targets the prevalent issue of scarce labeled data in medical imaging. We introduce a novel unsupervised few-shot learning algorithm, meticulously crafted for classifying periodontal diseases using a limited collection of dental panoramic radiographs.

pmc-11503911.title: Coupling of Spectrin Repeat Modules for the Assembly of Nanorods and Presentation of Protein Domains
pmc-11503911.creator: Klemen Mezgec, Jaka Snoj, Liza Ulčakar, Ajasja Ljubetič, Magda Tušek Žnidarič, Miha Škarabot, Roman Jerala
pmc-11503911.description: Modular protein engineering is a powerful approach for fabricating high-molecular-weight assemblies and biomaterials with nanoscale precision. Herein, we address the challenge of designing an extended nanoscale filamentous architecture inspired by the central rod domain of human dystrophin, which protects sarcolemma during muscle contraction and consists of spectrin repeats composed of three-helical bundles.

pmc-12581499.title: The effect of enzyme and protein containing toothpaste on gingival condition: a randomised controlled study
pmc-12581499.creator: Xiao Hu, PingNeng Zhang, Lu Zhang, Jane R Matheson, Shengnan Lin, Jianing N Sun, Cristina Delfanti, Jiangang Tian, Ashok K Gupta, Renuka Vasantharaghavan, Ruizhe Huang
pmc-12581499.description: BackgroundAccumulation of dental plaque can lead to gingival problems. A fluoride toothpaste containing naturally occurring enzymes and proteins has been shown to improve gingival health and reduce supragingival plaque in European populations. The objective of the current study was to evaluate the ability of this toothpaste to improve gingival condition and reduce supragingival plaque in an alternative study population.

pmc-12660958.title: Fabrication of curcumin-loaded emulgel and its application in low-calorie and functional cake
pmc-12660958.creator: Bita Mohammad Alami, Akram Arianfar, Ali Mohamadi Sani, Sara Naji Tabasi
pmc-12660958.description: In response to the growing need for healthier bakery products, this study aimed to partially replace fat with curcumin-loaded emulgels in cake formulations. Emulgels were prepared using Persian gum, sodium alginate, and inulin, with curcumin incorporated into sesame oil. Three concentrations of emulgel (30%, 50%, and 70% of fat) were incorporated into the cake mixture.

pmc-12705800.title: Vegetation type influences particulate organic matter storage along a low Arctic vegetation gradient
pmc-12705800.creator: Lewis Sauerland, Rica Wegner, Andrei Moise, Lukas Kohl, Jenie Gil, Birgit Wild
pmc-12705800.description: Permafrost soils constitute a large part of the terrestrial carbon pool that is vulnerable to future climate warming. Continued warming of the low Arctic is also leading to the encroachment of large shrubs and trees into tundra ecosystems with effects on microbial community composition, organic matter cycling and physical soil parameters.

pmc-13050965.title: Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment of 31 Children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae Necrotizing Pneumonia
pmc-13050965.creator: Zhaoxia Wang, Yuxin Zhao, Hongfang Liu
pmc-13050965.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to summarize the clinical characteristics and outcomes of necrotizing pneumonia caused by Mycobacterium pneumoniae in children.MethodsThe clinical features, accessory examinations, treatments, and prognoses of 31 children with M. pneumoniae necrotizing pneumonia admitted to our hospital between January 2020 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-13065587.title: Impact of Home-Based Respiratory Physiotherapy in Nusinersen-Treated Patients with Spinal Muscular Atrophy
pmc-13065587.creator: Moria Be’er, Lior Shperling, Mika Rochman, Israel Amirav, Michal Cahal, Revital Lavi, Efraim Sadot, Yotam Lior, Moran Lavie
pmc-13065587.description: IntroductionSpinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a progressive neuromuscular disorder associated with respiratory complications and reduced quality of life (QOL). Although disease-modifying therapies have altered the clinical course of SMA, the role of home-based respiratory physiotherapy as an adjunct to pharmacologic treatment remains underexplored.

pmc-13398708.title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Radiation Therapy Education: A Multi‐Modal Approach
pmc-13398708.creator: Laura Feighan, Leah Cramp, Debra Lee, Yolanda Surjan
pmc-13398708.description: IntroductionCritical workforce shortages in radiation oncology have led tertiary institutions to rapidly expand their radiation therapy (RT) student cohorts. The increase in students entering university created the challenge of scaling educational delivery while preserving the quantity and quality of learning essential for developing well‐prepared, competent clinicians.

pmc-13513181.title: Proteinuria Is Independently Associated with Impaired Gallbladder Emptying in Biopsy-Proven Glomerular Disease with Preserved Kidney Function: A Case–Control Ultrasonographic Study
pmc-13513181.creator: Simal Koksal Cevher, Hasan Tankut Koseoglu, Sabri Onur Ozden, Emre Cankaya, Ezgi Coskun Yenigun, Fatih Dede
pmc-13513181.description: Background/Objectives: Gallbladder emptying is primarily regulated by postprandial cholecystokinin release. In proteinuric glomerular diseases, renal loss of peptide hormones, hormone-binding proteins, or related regulatory proteins may affect biliary motility. However, gallbladder function has not been adequately investigated in individuals with proteinuric glomerular disease.

pmc-5753159.title: Global and Multi-National Prevalence of Fungal Diseases—Estimate Precision
pmc-5753159.creator: Felix Bongomin, Sara Gago, Rita O. Oladele et al.
pmc-5753159.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central). Fungal diseases kill more than 1.5 million and affect over a billion people. However, they are still a neglected topic by public health authorities even though most deaths from fungal diseases are avoidable. Serious fungal infections occur as a consequence of other health problem
